source_ground_truth:
At the checked-out commit, `main.py:main:21-76` is the callable entry point. It accepts an `ExecutionInput`; the `__main__` guard exits with instructions to construct one and call `main` (`main.py:__main__:118-122`). The tracked repository contains no CLI/API wrapper or in-repository caller of `main` (`git ls-files`; source references found by `rg`). `main` calls `contracts.validate_execution_input`, raises `ValueError` on errors, and only then creates `OrchestratorState` (`main.py:main:21-27`; `contracts.py:validate_execution_input:200-228`; `contracts.py:ExecutionInput:79-84`; `contracts.py:OrchestratorState:118-128`). Input validation requires verdict `PASS`, readiness true, a nonempty DSL and workspace root, required DSL sections/status consistency, at least one total cycle, and nonnegative retry/repair limits. It does not validate path lists or workspace-root existence (`contracts.py:validate_dsl_candidate:152-197`; `contracts.py:validate_execution_input:200-228`; `contracts.py:WorkspacePolicy:63-68`). Each loop iteration calls `codex_run.run_codex`, validates the result, stores it as `last_execution` and in history, calls `routing_system.route_decision`, validates the decision, and stores `last_route` (`main.py:main:29-46`; `main.py:_validate_or_stop_result:79-83`; `main.py:_validate_or_stop_decision:85-88`).

`run_codex` writes a temporary JSON spec containing the DSL, selected validator fields, and metadata, then invokes `subprocess.run` with the workspace root as `cwd`, captured text output, and a timeout (`codex_run.py:run_codex:22-75`; `codex_run.py:_write_temp_spec:126-155`). A nonempty metadata `codex_command` list is stringified and receives `--spec <path>`; otherwise the command is `codex exec --spec <path>`. A positive integer timeout is used, with a 300-second default (`codex_run.py:_build_codex_command:158-164`; `codex_run.py:_timeout_seconds:166-170`). Normal results use exit code zero for `SUCCESS`/`NONE` and nonzero for `FAILED` plus text-based classification. They include logs, heuristic test information, an empty `changed_files` list, and raw run/output/state fields (`codex_run.py:run_codex:48-75`; `codex_run.py:classify_error:180-212`; `codex_run.py:_extract_test_result:229-243`). The result validator checks status/error-type and exit-code consistency and rejects `tests.passed is None` when tests are marked as run. Although `TestResult.passed` is annotated `bool | None`, the validator does not runtime-check that a non-None value is actually a boolean (`contracts.py:TestResult:88-92`; `contracts.py:validate_execution_result:231-249`). Timeout and `FileNotFoundError` have separate result branches; the temp spec cleanup is attempted in `finally`, with `OSError` suppressed (`codex_run.py:run_codex:77-123`; `codex_run.py:_cleanup_temp_spec:173-177`).

Routing checks success first, then DSL blocking state, then the stuck-loop detector, and then error-specific branches (`routing_system.py:route_decision:19-118`). Test failures may retry, then repair or become fatal; spec conflicts may repair or regenerate; validation errors may repair or become fatal; Codex errors may retry or become fatal; environment and unknown errors are fatal. Router conditions depend on contract helpers for retry/repair budgets and DSL blocker checks (`routing_system.py:route_decision:42-118`; `routing_system.py:_dsl_has_blocking_state:121-139`; `routing_system.py` imports at 3-13; `contracts.py:contains_blocking_marker:139-149`; `contracts.py:can_retry_codex:270-274`; `contracts.py:can_repair_spec:277-281`). The stuck-loop detector takes the last two history errors and appends the current error (`routing_system.py:_detect_stuck_loop:142-149`). Since `main` appends the current result before routing, two consecutive matching failures can satisfy the three-element comparison. `main` returns state for success, regeneration, ask-user, and fatal routes; retry/repair update counters and continue, while exhausted budgets or the total-cycle limit end the loop. Repair only increments counters/version in this code; the comment says its hook will replace the DSL later, while each dispatch still passes the same `execution_input` (`main.py:main:48-76`; `main.py:_apply_retry_code_route:91-100`; `main.py:_apply_repair_spec_route:102-112`; `codex_run.py:_write_temp_spec:136-149`). The router does not emit `ASK_USER` in its checked-in branches (`routing_system.py:route_decision:33-118`), though `main` handles it. No persistent result writer appears in this orchestration path.
